source.title: Safety Anchor: Defending Harmful Fine-tuning via Geometric Bottlenecks
source.authors: Guoxin Lu; Le-Tian Sha; Qing Wang; Peijie Sun; Hao Zhou; Huaiyu Dai; Fu Xiao

record.file_problem: The paper is present in full. Some figure labels and plots are garbled in the extracted text; relevant prose and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the idea that refusal-related subspaces are largely orthogonal to benign reasoning as rationale for a defense, but it does not test the difference-in-means direction or the claim versions. Its Safety Bottleneck Regularization (SBR) results concern a different intervention.
record.gate_note: No experiment finds, removes, or adds the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. The paper's HFT, hidden-state anchoring, and geometric-clustering outcomes are recorded as findings about the broader subject, not as tests of the listed claim versions. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is a harmful-fine-tuning defense (SBR) that anchors final-layer hidden states of harmful prompts with an MSE loss. It never computes, ablates or adds a difference-in-means refusal direction. It cites Arditi et al. only as rationale: refusal subspaces are orthogonal to benign reasoning, and malicious queries cluster in a shared subspace. It neither tests the direction nor uses it as a tool, so 'uses_without_test/T4' overstates the link. 'cites_only/T6' fits better. Its random rank-1 LoRA attack concerns weight-space directions for restoring harmful outputs, not the activation-space refusal direction.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors also claim a single anchor suffices because malicious queries cluster in a shared final-layer subspace, which they attribute to refusal being mediated by a shared representation, citing Arditi et al.
record.recipe_differences: SBR uses an MSE constraint on final hidden states for selected high-risk prompts during fine-tuning. It does not find a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction or ablate or add one.
record.method_sensitivity: SBR outcomes vary with regularization depth and strength, anchor-set size, poison ratio, and model family. The authors report that intermediate-layer constraints remain ineffective relative to final-layer anchoring, λ values at or below 5 leave elevated HS, λ=200 lowers FA, and one anchor is reported to reduce HS to 6.

fits_no_version.finding: Under persistent harmful fine-tuning, SBR anchoring of final-layer hidden states keeps the harmful score below about 10 across Llama3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma1.1-7B, with utility near SFT. Constraints at intermediate layers fail (HS>50).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constraining final-layer hidden states of a few harmful anchor prompts preserves refusal under harmful fine-tuning, whereas intermediate-layer constraints are bypassed.

fits_no_version.finding: In base Llama3.1-8B final hidden states, unseen malicious queries sit near a harmful anchor (MSE≈2.5) and benign queries far from it (≈6.8). The clustering persists after SBR fine-tuning (Figure 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful prompts occupy a compact shared region of final-layer representation space, distinct from benign prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning confined to random frozen rank-1 LoRA directions restores harmfulness (HS>65) in all 8 trials. The weight updates have pairwise cosine below 0.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety can be undone through many nearly orthogonal weight-space directions during fine-tuning.

record.problems: The study's evidence concerns its own defense rather than the claimed direction. Main tables do not report error bars; three-run min-max variation is reported for the anchor-size figure. Some plot details are garbled in the extracted text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted under the 60-row limit. The paper's baseline-method results are not separately catalogued because they compare other HFT defenses, not the claimed direction or its intervention.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added. Refusal-rate effects and preserved capabilities under direction intervention are not measured.
No jailbreak is analysed for direction suppression, and there is no training against direction ablation. The fine-tuning attacks are not linked to the direction.
There is no test of affine, cone or multi-direction structure in activation space. The random weight-subspace attacks are about parameter updates.
Harm judgment is not separated from refusal.
Three model families are used, but no direction transfer is tested.
How refusal training shapes a direction is not studied.

missing.what: Random rank-1 subspace attack: HS>65 in 8 of 8 random directions, pairwise cosine <0.01. No row records it; it bears on no version, only on fits_no_version.

record.verdict_notes: The study's link to the claim is only by citation: refusal is orthogonal to benign reasoning, and the anchor clustering is read as consistent with a shared refusal subspace. These are interpretations, not tests. Downgrade the relation from uses_without_test/T4 to cites_only/T6. All rows remain 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, ablated, or added; the specified refusal and harmless-request outcomes are not tested.
No ablation is converted into a weight edit or evaluated as abliteration.
No attack is tested for suppressing the claimed direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
Hidden-state clustering is described, but the study does not test whether refusal requires an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
SBR is evaluated on multiple model families, but transfer of the claimed direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models is not tested.
The study varies HFT conditions, not the training that establishes refusal or whether that training creates a removable direction.
